title: ～さ — turns an adjective into a noun (“-ness”)
summary: Adding さ to an i-adjective stem or na-adjective stem makes a noun for the degree of that quality: 高い → 高さ, 重い → 重さ, 寒い → 寒さ.

patterns.gloss: い-adj minus い + さ (高い → 高さ)
Na-adj stem + さ (静か → 静かさ)

body.p: For i-adjectives drop the final い and add さ; いい becomes よさ. For na-adjectives, add さ directly to the stem.
Many are measurable quantities: 高さ, 重さ, 長さ, 広さ, 大きさ. Others show the strength of a feeling: 寒さ, 楽しさ. The result behaves as a noun and takes の, は, に and so on.

examples.ja: この山（やま）の高（たか）さは三千（さんぜん）メートルです。
examples.romaji: Kono yama no takasa wa sanzen mētoru desu.
examples.tr: The height of this mountain is 3,000 meters.

examples.ja: この荷物（にもつ）の重（おも）さは十（じゅう）キロだ。
examples.romaji: Kono nimotsu no omosa wa jukkiro da.
examples.tr: The weight of this luggage is ten kilos.

examples.ja: 冬（ふゆ）の朝（あさ）の寒（さむ）さには驚（おどろ）いた。
examples.romaji: Fuyu no asa no samusa ni wa odoroita.
examples.tr: I was surprised by the coldness of a winter morning.

pitfalls: いい becomes よさ, not いさ.
Not every adjective takes さ naturally; learn the common pairs.
